title: An OpenID Connect relying application sends a browser to Mandate and gets an authorization code back, signing the browser in upstream only when it holds no Mandate session
summary: A relying application (an application, or a gateway in front of one) speaks OpenID Connect to Mandate as its OpenID Provider. It sends the browser to the authorization endpoint with `scope=openid` and no Mandate-specific parameter. A browser with no Mandate session is sent to the organization's upstream identity provider and, at the relying-party callback, the authorization request it came with is resumed: the browser returns to the application's registered redirect with a code and the exact state, and holds a host-only session cookie. A browser that holds the cookie is answered the code without an upstream round trip. These are steps 1 to 4 of the road; the token, ID token, refresh and logout steps are named below as gaps with their owners.

serves.requirement_words: An app behind an Envoy Gateway `oidc` SecurityPolicy works unchanged when its issuer URL moves from

parties.role: The process this repository builds: `mandate-control-plane serve`, acting as the OpenID Provider toward the relying application and as the relying party toward the upstream identity provider.

delivers.statement: An authorization request names a registered client of either type and an exact redirect; PKCE is offered whole or not at all; an OpenID Connect request names no target and its code is for the resource server whose `client_id` names the client.
A resource server may name the client it is the audience of, which is how an OpenID Connect request that names no target is resolved to one.
The authorization endpoint, reached by a browser with the host-only session cookie, a bearer session proof, or no session at all.
The upstream identity provider's return; for a sign-in the authorization endpoint started, it resumes that request and sets the session cookie.

A browser with no session is sent upstream and returns to the client's redirect with a code, the exact state and a `__Host-mandate-session` cookie that is `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Path=/`.
The cookie skips the upstream round trip; `prompt=login` forces one; `prompt=none` with no usable session answers `login_required` at the redirect.

relies_on.statement: The redirect the relying application registered, against which every answer of the authorization endpoint is sent.

parties.role: The application, or the gateway in front of it, that sends browsers to Mandate's authorization endpoint as an OpenID Connect client.

delivers.statement: Its callback, registered byte for byte.
It sends `scope=openid`, a fresh `state` and `nonce`, and an S256 code challenge on every authorization request.
delivers.refuted_by: a request without `openid` and without a target is refused `invalid_scope`; a public client's request without a challenge is refused before anything is sent upstream.

delivers.statement: It checks the `state` it gets back before it uses the code.
delivers.refuted_by: nothing here observes it: the state is returned exactly as received, and whether it was checked is visible only in the application.

relies_on.statement: The endpoint it sends browsers to.

parties.role: The organization's external OIDC identity provider, configured as the connection's relying-party IdP.

delivers.statement: The callback Mandate registered with it and the reference to the client secret it issued.
It returns the browser to the registered callback with a code and the exact state, and signs an ID token carrying the nonce Mandate sent.
delivers.refuted_by: the callback is refused (`StateMismatch` or `NonceMismatch` on the operator's stream) and no session is opened.

relies_on.statement: The callback it returns browsers to.

parties.role: The person whose browser is sent between the relying application, Mandate and the upstream identity provider.

delivers.statement: Their browser keeps the `__Host-mandate-session` and `__Host-mandate-rp` cookies and returns them to Mandate's origin.
delivers.refuted_by: a browser that drops the binding cookie has its callback refused (`StateMismatch`); one that drops the session cookie is sent upstream on every authorization.

relies_on.statement: The endpoint the relying application sends their browser to.

parties.role: Whoever writes the flag documents the deployment is started with.

delivers.statement: The client the resource server is the audience of, so an OpenID Connect request naming no target resolves to it.

steps.statement: The relying application is recorded as a client of the organization, public or confidential, with its exact redirects and whether it must use PKCE.
The relying application's resource server is registered naming its client; a client that does not resolve, is disabled or is another organization's is refused.

steps.when: first authorization of a browser, and every `prompt=login`
steps.statement: A browser with no usable session is signed in through the organization's one relying-party connection, and the authorization request it came with is held for the callback.
The code is issued for the session the cookie or the resumed sign-in names and returned to the exact redirect with the exact state.

routes.statement: The authorization endpoint. A browser's session is the host-only cookie; none sends it upstream, and `prompt=none` with none is `login_required`.
The relying-party callback, which resumes the authorization request that started the sign-in.

fields.statement: Public or confidential. A public client always uses PKCE; a confidential one when `pkce_required` holds.
The redirects compared byte for byte; every answer of the authorization endpoint after the client is validated is sent to the one presented.
Whether a confidential client must offer PKCE. Defaults to true.
The client this resource server is the audience of. It must resolve to an enabled client of the same organization, seeded by a `--client` document.
How long a session lasts, and so how long the browser keeps the session cookie (`Max-Age`). Defaults to PT8H.

standards.governs: refusals after the client and redirect are validated are sent to the redirect with the exact state
PKCE is offered whole or not at all, and a public client always offers it
the host-only `__Host-` session cookie and its attributes

not_yet_true.gap: the authorization endpoint's command is not realized by an accounting crate
not_yet_true.costs: Nothing a browser sees: the adapter answers the road end to end. The command's coverage row stays deferred, so its accepted and denied scenarios are not decided by the conformance suite.

not_yet_true.gap: a confidential client that omits PKCE is admitted by the client check and refused at code issuance
not_yet_true.costs: A relying application registered with `pkce_required: false` must still send a challenge.
not_yet_true.today: Code issuance records a challenge on every code; scenario `oidc-authorize-confidential-without-pkce` is unsupported.

not_yet_true.gap: no ID token, no client authentication at the token endpoint, no refresh and no logout
not_yet_true.costs: The relying application gets a code it can redeem for a Mandate credential but no ID token; steps 5 onward of the road are not served.
not_yet_true.today: The token endpoint answers the authorization-code grant for public clients only.
